name: Audio Reverb Consistency
description: Analyzes audio reverberation patterns for environmental consistency — AI-generated audio may have mismatched or absent reverb characteristics.
mechanism:
This method detects audio manipulation by analyzing the consistency of reverberation characteristics throughout a recording:

1. **Reverberation Fingerprint Extraction**: The method extracts reverberation parameters from speech segments using blind RT60 estimation. For each voiced segment, it computes: RT60 (reverberation time), direct-to-reverberant ratio (DRR), early-to-late energy ratio (C50/C80), and the spectral envelope of the late reverb tail. These parameters form a reverberation fingerprint that characterizes the acoustic space. In authentic single-room recordings, this fingerprint remains stable across all speech segments. The method uses the maximum likelihood estimation technique of Löllmann et al. (2010) applied to the temporal energy decay of speech offsets.

2. **Intra-Recording Reverb Stability**: The method divides the audio into overlapping analysis windows (3 seconds, 75% overlap) and computes reverb parameters for each window. A consistency metric is calculated as the coefficient of variation of RT60 and DRR across all windows. In authentic recordings from a single location, RT60 variance is typically < 0.05s (CV < 10%). Spliced audio from different locations or AI-generated audio with inconsistent room modeling shows reverb parameter variations exceeding these thresholds. The method also detects abrupt reverb transitions — step changes in RT60 > 0.15s between adjacent windows — which indicate edit points.

3. **Early Reflection Pattern Analysis**: The pattern of early reflections (first 50ms after direct sound) encodes the geometry of the recording space — reflection arrival times correspond to wall distances, and their spectral content reflects surface materials. The method estimates the early reflection pattern using sparse deconvolution and verifies its consistency across speech segments. Authentic recordings maintain a stable early reflection pattern (same room geometry). AI-generated audio typically lacks early reflections entirely (anechoic quality) or includes generic reverb that doesn't exhibit the discrete early reflection structure of a real room.

4. **Reverb-Visual Coherence Scoring**: When video accompanies the audio, the method cross-references reverb characteristics with the visible environment. It checks: (a) outdoor visual scenes should have RT60 < 0.2s, (b) small rooms should have RT60 ∈ [0.2, 0.5s], (c) large halls should have RT60 ∈ [0.5, 2.0s], (d) reverb should change when the speaker moves between rooms. A coherence score quantifies the agreement between visual scene acoustics prediction and measured reverb parameters. Low coherence scores flag potential audio manipulation or AI generation.
parameters:
Analysis window: 3 seconds, 75% overlap
RT60 estimation method: maximum likelihood decay rate
RT60 consistency threshold: CV < 10%
Abrupt transition threshold: ΔRT60 > 0.15s
DRR consistency threshold: CV < 15%
Early reflection window: 0–50 ms
Late reverb window: 50–500 ms
Spectral analysis bands: 8 octave bands (125 Hz – 8 kHz)
Minimum voiced segments: 10
Sample rate: ≥ 16 kHz
accuracy: 78–86% accuracy detecting reverb inconsistencies in manipulated or AI-generated audio. Intra-recording RT60 consistency achieves AUC of 0.84 for splice detection. Early reflection analysis provides F1-score of 0.80 for distinguishing real room reverb from synthetic reverb. Performance strongest for indoor recordings with clear reverberation; weaker for outdoor or heavily processed audio.
source: Löllmann, H. W., Yilmaz, E., Vary, P. (2010). An Improved Algorithm for Blind Reverberation Time Estimation. Proceedings of IWAENC, 1–4.
useCase: Detecting spliced audio recordings by identifying reverb discontinuities. Verifying that audio was recorded in the claimed environment. Identifying AI-generated audio that lacks realistic room acoustic modeling. Forensic authentication of recorded evidence — conversations, confessions, phone calls.
strengths:
• Reverberation is physically determined by the recording environment — difficult to forge
• Consistency analysis requires no reference recording from the claimed room
• Early reflection analysis captures room geometry information absent in synthetic audio
• Robust to content changes — reverb is independent of what is being said
• Can pinpoint exact splice locations via abrupt reverb transitions
limitations:
• Close-microphone recordings capture minimal reverb — limited analysis sensitivity
• Professional audio with reverb post-processing may appear inconsistent
• AI systems with room impulse response modeling can produce consistent reverb
• Outdoor recordings naturally have minimal reverb — limited discriminative information
• Moving speakers in a room cause natural DRR variation that may trigger false positives
